questiontext.text:
{@ctx@} is a triangular prism ABCDEF. The base ABED is horizontal, the face BCFE is vertical and ACFD is the sloping face. AB = {@aa@}, BC = {@rr@} and AD = {@bb@} {@un@}.

[[jsxgraph width="360px" height="280px"]] (function() { var b = JXG.JSXGraph.initBoard(divid, {boundingbox: [-1.0, 4.9, 8.8, -2.7], axis: false, grid: false, keepaspectratio: true, showNavigation: false, showCopyright: false, pan: {enabled: false}, zoom: {enabled: false}}); // oblique projection: receding edges at 30 degrees, half length function P(x, y, z) { return [x + 0.5*y*Math.cos(Math.PI/6), z + 0.5*y*Math.sin(Math.PI/6)]; } var solid = {strokeColor: '#000000', strokeWidth: 2, fixed: true, highlight: false}; var hid = {strokeColor: '#000000', strokeWidth: 1.5, dash: 2, fixed: true, highlight: false}; var dot = {strokeColor: '#000000', strokeWidth: 1.5, dash: 1, fixed: true, highlight: false}; var tx = {fixed: true, highlight: false, useMathJax: false, fontSize: 15, anchorX: 'middle', anchorY: 'middle'}; var cx = 3.87, cy = 1.0; function lab(Q, s) { var dx = Q[0]-cx, dy = Q[1]-cy, r = Math.sqrt(dx*dx+dy*dy) || 1; b.create('text', [Q[0]+0.42*dx/r, Q[1]+0.42*dy/r, s], tx); } function seg(Q, R, o) { b.create('segment', [Q, R], o); } function mark(Q, R, S) { // right-angle mark at Q between QR and QS function u(X) { var dx = X[0]-Q[0], dy = X[1]-Q[1], r = Math.sqrt(dx*dx+dy*dy); return [0.3*dx/r, 0.3*dy/r]; } var a = u(R), c = u(S); b.create('polygon', [[Q[0]+a[0], Q[1]+a[1]], [Q[0]+a[0]+c[0], Q[1]+a[1]+c[1]], [Q[0]+c[0], Q[1]+c[1]]], {fixed: true, highlight: false, fillOpacity: 0, vertices: {visible: false}, borders: {strokeColor: '#000000', strokeWidth: 1, fixed: true, highlight: false}}); } // ramp: triangular prism ABCDEF, base ABED horizontal, BCFE vertical, ACFD sloping (shape only) var A = P(0,0,0), B = P(6,0,0), C = P(6,0,2), D = P(0,4,0), E = P(6,4,0), F = P(6,4,2); seg(A,B,solid); seg(B,C,solid); seg(C,A,solid); seg(B,E,solid); seg(C,F,solid); seg(E,F,solid); // hidden corner D: its three edges dashed seg(A,D,hid); seg(D,E,hid); seg(D,F,hid); mark(B, A, C); mark(E, D, F); lab(A,'A'); lab(B,'B'); lab(C,'C'); lab(D,'D'); lab(E,'E'); lab(F,'F'); })(); [[/jsxgraph]]

The diagram is not drawn to scale.

(a) Find the angle between AF and the base ABED.

[[input:ans1]] \(^\circ\) [[validation:ans1]] [[feedback:prt1]]

(b) Which of these lines on the sloping face makes the greatest angle with the base?

[[input:ans2]] [[validation:ans2]] [[feedback:prt2]]

Give lengths correct to 2 decimal places and angles correct to 1 decimal place. Keep full calculator accuracy until the final answer.

generalfeedback.text:
(a) F is vertically above E, so the projection of AF on the base is AE, the diagonal of the base: \(\mathrm{AE}^2 = {@aa@}^2 + {@bb@}^2 = {@SE@}\). Triangle AEF has a right angle at E, so \(\tan \mathrm{FAE} = \frac{{@rr@}}{\sqrt{{@SE@}}}\) and angle FAE = \({@d1(th)@}^\circ\).

(b) AF, AC and CD all rise {@rr@} {@un@}, but AC does it over the shortest horizontal distance, AB = {@aa@} {@un@}: AC, at right angles to the bottom edge AD, is a line of greatest slope (\({@d1(slp)@}^\circ\)). AD is horizontal.

questiondescription.text:
Three-Dimensional Geometry: angles on a ramp

Grade 12 CBE Core 2.4: Find the angle between a diagonal of the sloping face of a ramp and the base, and identify a line of greatest slope.

Core

This question is adapted from Chapter 34, Test yourself, question T1(c) of Ling, J., Scruton, P., Shilton, S. and West, H., SMP GCSE Mathematics: Higher 2 for AQA, Edexcel and OCR two-tier GCSE mathematics, Cambridge University Press, 2007: a ramp-shaped prism with right-angled ends, new contexts and numbers, a line-of-greatest-slope part added, randomised, with named feedback.

INNODEMS CBC Grade 12 Mathematics, first draft by Ben Davies, 2026. Aligned to the KICD Senior School Curriculum Design, Core Mathematics Grade 12 (draft).

feedbackvariables.text: okr: is(ans1 > 0 and ans1 < 90); rdn: float(ans1*%pi/180); aev: if okr then float(rr/tan(rdn)) else NA;

truefeedback.text: That is the angle of AC, which goes straight up the slope. AF goes across it: F is above E, so the projection of AF is the diagonal of the base, not AB.
You used AD as the projection. F is above E, not above D, so the projection of AF is a diagonal of the base.
That is angle AFE, at F, between AF and the vertical edge FE.
Your calculator is set to radians. Set it to degrees (DEG) and work out the angle again.
Your answer is close but not accurate to 1 decimal place. Keep full calculator accuracy until the end, then round the angle once.

falsefeedback.text:
[[if test="okr"]]

F is {@rr@} {@un@} above the base. With your angle, the projection of AF on the base would be {@d2(aev)@} {@un@} long. Which line in the base ABED is the projection of AF, and how long is it?

[[else]]

An angle between two lines, or between a line or plane and a plane, is between \(0^\circ\) and \(90^\circ\). Check your working and your calculator mode.

[[/if]]

[[if test="kAD"]]

AD is horizontal: it lies in the base, so its angle with the base is \(0^\circ\). Look for a line that climbs.

[[else]][[if test="kAF"]]

AF climbs {@rr@} {@un@}, but it crosses the slope at a slant: its projection on the base is the diagonal AE, longer than either side of the base. Is there a line that climbs the same {@rr@} {@un@} over a shorter horizontal distance?

[[else]]

CD climbs {@rr@} {@un@}, but it crosses the slope at a slant: its projection on the base is the diagonal BD, longer than either side of the base. Is there a line that climbs the same {@rr@} {@un@} over a shorter horizontal distance?

[[/if]][[/if]]
